data.body:
CORRECTION to the root cause I recorded above — mine was the smaller half, and I am superseding it.

I wrote that the mechanism is four pytest-xdist workers against a four-slot semaphore, i.e. *the
suite exhausting its own gate admission*. That is true and reproducible, but it does not explain
the observation that actually matters: running the failing tests ALONE, on a host with no other
tests running, still produced 14 failures.

## The deeper fact: the four slots are HOST-GLOBAL

`gate_admission._slot_dir()` resolves to `store_root()/locks`, and `store_root()` resolves to
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` or else `tempfile.gettempdir()` — **one directory shared by every worktree,
every session, and every rebar process on the machine.**

An agent listed the live holders during a failing run:

    gate-slot-0   PID 50765   /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-e54e-shims      rebar verify-completion
    gate-slot-1   PID 6229    /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-f773-cli        rebar review-plan
    gate-slot-2   PID 20256   /Users/joeoakhart/rebar                   (global rebar-dev build)
    gate-slot-3   PID 89566   /Users/joeoakhart/janitor-038d-config     rebar ...

All four held by OTHER SESSIONS running real 15-20 minute LLM gate operations. The agent's own
pytest worker count at that moment was **zero**. So the tests were not competing with other tests —
they were competing with production gate work that was not running any test at all.

Two consequences follow that my version missed:

1. **"Run it in isolation" does not isolate.** The slot directory is outside the test session's
   control, so a serial re-run on a quiet-looking box still fails if four gate ops are open
   elsewhere on the machine. That is why the agent's first isolation run showed 14 failures and
   would have read as a real defect.
2. **The gate fails closed WITHOUT WAITING.** A test needing a slot dies instantly rather than
   queueing, so there is no backpressure — the failure is immediate and total rather than slow.

## Demonstrated fix direction

Re-running the same tests with a private `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` (its own `locks/`, its own four
slots) gave **71 passed / 0 failed**. So pointing the test fixture at a per-session slot directory
resolves it without touching the production limit.

## Revised CI consequence

My earlier note said the gating cell can produce a spurious `Verified -1` because 4 xdist workers
meet 4 slots. Still true. But the sharper statement is: **these tests are red whenever four real
gate operations are in flight anywhere on the box, including in CI if a runner is ever shared.**
The trigger is not confined to the suite's own parallelism.

Recording this as a correction rather than an addition, because a reader who acts only on my
earlier comment would fix the worker/slot ratio and still have red tests.
